title: Episode 95: Shared α-helix chimeraffibodies enable linker-free bispecific protein design
itunes_title: Shared α-helix chimeraffibodies enable linker-free bispecific protein design
description:
**Monday Immune Engager** — our weekly pick from the latest immune-engager digest.

**[Shared α-helix chimeraffibodies enable linker-free bispecific protein design](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chembiol.2026.09.022)**

*Cell Chemical Biology, 2026*

DOI: [10.1016/j.chembiol.2026.09.022](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chembiol.2026.09.022)

**Question:** Can two α-helical binding domains be fused by sharing a single helix instead of a flexible linker, without destroying either paratope?

**Answer:** Yes for one lineage: the lead construct bound albumin at ~14.3 pM and HER2 at 610 pM, matching parental affinities, with a rigid single-conformation structure by MD. A second lineage initially failed, rescued only after diagnosing one electrostatic clash; no experimental structure of the dual-bound complex exists.

**Three takeaways**

1. The strongest evidence is a failure case: one glutamate-to-glycine substitution restored albumin affinity ~100-fold (121 nM to 1.23 nM).
2. Binding data are solid, but in vivo gains are thin — a 110.2 vs 96.2-hour tumor half-life difference came from only 3 mice per group.
3. Immunogenicity claims rest on MHC-II prediction and acute cytokine assays, not repeat-dose antibody data — weaker evidence than the headline implies.

source_metadata.title: Shared α-helix chimeraffibodies enable linker-free bispecific protein design
source_metadata.abstract: Small protein scaffolds enable precise targeting but often rely on flexible linkers that increase conformational heterogeneity and immunogenic liabilities. Here we develop Chimeraffibodies (CABs), a linker-free bispecific scaffold class that encodes interdomain geometry through seamless α-helix sharing. CABs are designed by AlphaSync, a structure-design framework that defines domain orientation through closed-form exhaustive local rigid-body superposition and ProteinMPNN-based sequence refinement. Using HER2-binding affibody and an albumin-binding domain, we generated 861CM, which preserved parental paratopes while enforcing a defined shared-helix architecture. Structural, biophysical and cellular analyses demonstrated stable assembly, cooperative target recruitment and retained affinity, with HSA binding of ∼14.3 pM and HER2 binding of 610 pM in the albumin-bound state. In vivo imaging revealed sustained tumor localization, reduced hepatic and renal background and improved organ-to-tumor contrast. CABs establish helix sharing as a geometry-encoded strategy for generating compact, homogeneous, and pharmacokinetically optimized bispecific proteins.
